subject: Living-room storage around real routines
hook: Plan living-room storage around your evenings, not a catalogue
ig:
Plan living-room storage around your evenings, not around a catalogue photo.

Before we draw anything for an alcove or a media wall, we ask what actually happens in the room. Five routines come up again and again:

The drop zone: keys, post and chargers that land on the nearest flat surface.
The toy reset: the faster tidying is, the more often it happens. Deep low drawers win.
Film night: remotes, controllers and throws want a closed cupboard within reach of the sofa.
The reading chair: one open shelf beside it does more than a full bookcase across the room.
Hosting: games and spare glasses can live higher up, because you need them monthly, not daily.

The rule underneath it all: daily things low and close, occasional things high and away.

Save this for when you plan your living room, and see our options via the link in bio.
fb:
Most living rooms don't have a storage problem, they have a 'where does this go?' problem.

When we plan living-room furniture, we start with how you use the room. Where do the keys get dropped? How long does the toy tidy-up take? Where do the remotes and blankets end up on film night?

Once you know that, the layout almost designs itself: everyday things low and close to where they're used, occasional things higher up and behind doors.
